newsitem.title: USA: Sprint ordered to rehire 177 workers.
newsitem.headline: Sprint ordered to rehire 177 workers.

text.p: The government ordered Sprint Corp. to rehire and pay full back pay and benefits to 177 workers whose San Francisco telemarketing office was shut down during a union organising drive in 1994.
Sprint challenged the ruling by the National Labour Relations Board in an appeal filed with a federal court, a spokesman for the Kansas City, Mo.-based telecommunications company said.

In the decision released Monday, the NLRB ruled that Sprint's sudden closing of the marketing office in July 1994, just one week before a scheduled union election, violated federal law, the Communications Workers of America said.
The office, which employed mostly Hispanic women, was called La Conexion Familiar, Spanish for "The Family Connection."
The union said the NLRB ruled in favour of an appeal by the union of a decision by an administrative law judge.
It said the board rejected Sprint's contention that it closed the office because it was losing money.
The NLRB ordered Sprint to rehire the workers and give them "a position in its existing operations that is substantially equivalent to the employee's former position," the union said.
Sprint must pay appropriate moving expenses and pay them compensation for wages and benefits, plus interest, from the date of the closing to the date they are rehired, it said.
Sprint spokesman Bill White said, "We find it surprising that it (the board) did not uphold the earlier decisions," referring to two rulings in Sprint's favour.
White said those rulings found the company's reasons for closing the office -- financial losses and a dwindling customer base -- to be legitimate.
The Communications Workers of America represents more than 600,000 workers in telecommunications, television, journalism and publishing and the public-service sector.
Sprint stock dropped 75 cents to $39.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
